title: Paul Gayten in his band and the Hurricane
summary: Paul Gayten sang in his band, then left for Robin Hood and recorded for Deluxe.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Yeah. Any other recordings you remember? I mean from that early period?
Oh yeah, I recorded with Paul Gaten too. Oh, with Paul.
Now that's somebody I really admire. Did you know?
Now you know when Paul first came to New Orleans, when he got out of the city, he played with my band.
Yeah. And I was playing at a place called The Hurricane. Oh you worked at The Hurricane.

On Louison Avenue. No, on Claiborne and Louison. Claiborne and around 3rd. Yeah. No, Claiborne and Louison Avenue. So Paul played with me and he started singing that number, I'm true, because I'm crazy over you. And everybody was crazy about him singing that thing. So this guy, Benny Ross, who had a place to call it Robin Hood, he heard Paul and he hired Paul to come play at his place and say I want you to get your own band. So Paul left my band to go to get his own band. And everybody was talking about the truth and how much they liked it. So he recorded that for Deluxe.
That was a big hit. Yeah. When you were working with Paul, who was, it was you and Paul and who else was in that band at The Hurricane? You said it was at the-
Oh no, no, no, I didn't play with him at The Hurricane.
Because he left my band to get his own band. And I started playing at the Dewdrop. So he played, I started playing at the Dewdrops. With my own band.
